title: Frontend: Topological Sort (DFS)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Topological Sort (DFS). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}) for vertices 0..count-1, directed edges [from,to]. DFS vertices and neighbors in ascending order; return reversed completion order. A cycle throws Cycle.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use three visitation states: unseen, active on the DFS path, and complete.
alternativeApproaches: Return a cycle witness and distinguish an edge to an active node from an edge to an already completed node.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Disconnected vertices; self-loop; cycle.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
